hypothesis.statement: The host is already about 1024 pending descriptors per outer stream, so a larger submission window cannot expose future same-stream kernels. Forking Q, K, and V after pre-RMS changes the dependency-ready frontier from at most two outer-stream heads to six sibling grids while preserving the exact Stage07 id70 arithmetic.
hypothesis.scope: exact B29/CC10.3/19x19/FP16/NHWC trunk Q/K/V only; heads and reduced precision are excluded
hypothesis.expected_mechanism: The 126-block, one-SM, 0.85-wave id70 grids cannot co-reside on one SM because each CTA uses 215.04 KiB, but six ready grids give the scheduler more partial-wave packing choices across otherwise-free SMs. Success requires lower interval union, not lower summed kernel work.

implementation.startup_contract: Requires cudaSm103Backend, cudaSm103ReusePortableTactics, exact CC10.3/B29/FP16/NHWC, cudaUseProjectionGemmLt, the complete fixed id70 tuple, and no strided/fused QKV hook.
implementation.ownership: Each outer ComputeHandle owns one Sm120Model. That model owns two persistent nonblocking aux streams, two independent LtMatmulState objects, two independent cuBLASLt handles and private workspace allocations, plus three timing-disabled events. No resource is shared across outer lanes or K/V branches.
dag_per_attention: K and V aux streams wait ready
Q launches through the retained primary id70 state
K and V launch through their independent exact-id70 states
aux streams record K-done and V-done
primary waits both done events before the existing RoPE and FA4
implementation.numeric_semantics: All projections retain CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F, FP16 inputs/outputs, FP16 alpha=1/beta=0, column-major M384/N10469/K384 layouts, the complete id70 tuple, and zero algorithm workspace bytes.
implementation.runtime_error_checks: Every Lt launch and event API checks its direct return status. The noexcept teardown directly checks both cudaStreamSynchronize return values and uses Global::fatalError on failure; it never throws from a destructor and never reads or clears unrelated thread-local CUDA error state.

lifetime_root_cause_case_study.trigger: replaynn creates one two-handle warmup evaluator, destroys it, then creates a second two-handle output evaluator in the same process
lifetime_root_cause_case_study.initial_result: The first implementation passed repeated 300-forward benchmarknn processes but both normal and CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 replaynn failed in the second handle generation with SM103 FA4 LAUNCH_FAILED (-4).
lifetime_root_cause_case_study.root_cause: ComputeHandle member destruction is reverse declaration order: Sm103Model was destroyed first and unloaded the native FA4 module; Sm120Model synchronized and destroyed its auxiliary streams only afterward. The primary join was not an acceptable cross-owner teardown proof.
lifetime_root_cause_case_study.fix: ComputeHandle::~ComputeHandle now makes the device current and explicitly calls noexcept Sm120Model::synchronizeSm103QKVAux before member destruction can unload Sm103 FA4. The method directly checks both stream-synchronize statuses and terminates through Global::fatalError on failure, so no exception can escape the implicit-noexcept destructor. Sm120Model still repeats no-throw synchronization during resource cleanup as defense in depth.
lifetime_root_cause_case_study.proof: With no FA4 bridge change and no CUDA error clearing, the same 8192-row two-generation replay completed and wrote 445383368 bytes. All direct Lt/event API checks and both teardown synchronizations passed.
lifetime_root_cause_case_study.test_pin: python/tests/test_sm103_qkv_aux_contract.py asserts that ComputeHandle invokes synchronizeSm103QKVAux in its destructor body before reverse member destruction reaches Sm103Model, and pins noexcept plus fatal handling of both synchronization failures.

activation_proof.marker: SM103 portable backend: QKV aux streams active, tactic=cublaslt-id70-q-primary-kv-aux2-b29

short_symmetric.method: same binary, exact B29/S2, 50 warmups and 300 timed forwards, A-B-B-A

whole_graph_nsys.method: same final binary; control and aux each use 20 warmups plus 50 timed forwards per outer stream; steady analysis selects the last 50 of exactly 72 initial-convolution markers on each primary stream

full_trace_including_initial_plan_timing.interpretation: The 36 extra launches are exactly nine first-plan timing launches for each of four aux Lt states. Full-trace kernel sum falls 0.3422%, union falls 2.6745%, and overlap rises 3.6481%.

steady_last_50_per_outer_stream.exact_dag_accounting: Across 100 forwards there are 3300 attention boundaries. Candidate minus control is exactly 9900 event records (3 per boundary) and 13200 waits (4 per boundary). K/V move exactly 6600 kernels from the two primary streams to four aux streams; launch count remains identical.
steady_last_50_per_outer_stream.result: Kernel sum falls 0.3764%, union falls 2.8257%, and overlap rises 3.7870%. QKV summed service grows 8.9741%, but its union falls 26.3493%; the optimization is entirely dependency-DAG scheduling, not a faster GEMM.

whole_graph_nsys.ncu_reuse: No new NCU run is needed because every runtime marker proves the complete Stage07 id70 tuple and the kernel family is unchanged. Stage07 NCU remains the physical resource proof: grid126/block256/one-SM/0.85 waves/96 registers/215.04 KiB/no spills.

stage07_comparison.interpretation: The arithmetic tuple is unchanged, but the altered resource schedule changes downstream accumulated FP16 rounding in the already-known schedule-sensitive fused graph. The difference is numerically tiny and the fixed FP32/TRT implementation-error gates pass.

decision.reason: The candidate preserves all 9900 steady QKV launches and the fixed id70 kernel, but exposes a six-grid ready frontier. NSYS proves lower QKV and whole-graph union; replay and long testing pass after fixing the cross-owner teardown lifetime bug.
